case_name: State Of N.C.T. Of Delhi v Ajay Kumar Tyagi
respondent:
Ajay Kumar Tyagi
Supreme Court of India

31 August 2012
CRIMINAL APPEAL No. 1334 OF 2012 (@ SLP(Crl.) No. 1383 of 2010)
The Judgment was delivered by : Chandramauli Kr. Prasad, J.
1.   Ajay Kumar Tyagi, at the relevant time, was working as a Junior Engineer with the Delhi Jal Board. Surinder Singh, a Constable with the Delhi Police applied to the Delhi Jal Board, hereinafter referred to as 'the Board', for water connection in the name of his wife Sheela Devi. The application for grant of water connection was cleared by the Assistant Engineer and the file was sent to said Ajay Kumar Tyagi (hereinafter refered to as ' the accused ').
2.   Constable Surinder Singh lodged a report with the Anti Corruption Branch alleging that the accused demanded bribe of Rs. 2000/- for clearing the file and a sum of Rs. 1000/- was to be paid initially and the balance amount after the clearance of file. On the basis of the information lodged, a trap was laid and, according to the
facts: Ajay Kumar Tyagi was working as a Junior Engineer with the Delhi Jal Board.
Surinder Singh applied for water connection in the name of his wife Sheela Devi and the file was sent to Ajay Kumar Tyagi.
Constable Surinder Singh lodged a report with the Anti Corruption Branch alleging that Ajay Kumar Tyagi demanded bribe for clearing the file.
A trap was laid and according to the prosecution, Ajay Kumar Tyagi demanded and accepted the bribe of Rs. 1000/-.
The accused was put on trial and charges were framed by the Special Judge.
In respect of the same incident, a departmental proceeding was also initiated against the accused and the Article of Charges was served on him.
The enquiry officer conducted the departmental inquiry and submitted its report.

The High Court quashed the criminal proceedings and observed that if the charge could not be proved in the departmental proceedings where the standard of proof was much lower, it is very unlikely that the same charge could be proved in a criminal trial where the standard of proof is quite stringent comparatively.
issues: Whether the prosecution against an accused, notwithstanding his exoneration on the identical charge in the departmental proceeding could continue or not?
petitioner_arguments: The assumption on which the High Court had proceeded that the accused has been exonerated in the disciplinary proceeding is unfounded on facts.

The inquiry officer's report was yet to be considered and nothing prevented the disciplinary authority to disagree with the finding of the inquiry officer and punish the accused after following the due process of law.
respondent_arguments: At such a distance of time, the disciplinary authority is precluded from passing any order and the disciplinary proceeding shall be deemed to have been ended in exoneration.
court_reasoning: The disciplinary authority is not bound by the conclusion of the inquiry officer and can differ with the conclusion and record a finding of guilt and punish the delinquent employee.
As the order of the High Court is founded on an erroneous premise, the same cannot be allowed to stand.
In the light of the direction of the High Court, the departmental proceeding has to be reopened and kept in abeyance till the conclusion of the criminal case.
holding: The impugned order of the High Court suffers from an apparent illegality and deserves to be set aside.
The order of the disciplinary authority founded on that is also set aside.
The departmental proceeding has to be reopened and kept in abeyance till the conclusion of the criminal case.
